_about: Estimated API list prices in USD per 1M tokens. Subscription plans (Claude Max, ChatGPT plans) are not billed per token, so amounts are for comparison and locating cost only. To update: edit the numbers below, set read_date and keep the sources.

_rules: usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens -> cache_write_5m, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens -> cache_write_1h; if the breakdown is missing, treat all cache_creation_input_tokens as 5m.
input_tokens = uncached input; cache_read_input_tokens -> cache_read; output_tokens (thinking included) -> output.
usage.inference_geo == 'us' multiplies every category by 1.1 (Claude 4.6 and later).
Claude 4.6+ (except Haiku 5.5) bill the full 1M context at standard prices.
Haiku 5.5 is tiered per request by prompt length = input + cache_read + cache_write: <=100000 uses the first tier, >100000 the second.
usage.service_tier other than 'standard' (fast mode) is not priced here; count it at standard prices and flag it.
Models not in this table are unpriced (amount unknown, tokens still counted). Local models cost 0.

_rules: token_count.info.last_token_usage per model response: input_tokens INCLUDES cached_input_tokens and cache_write_input_tokens; uncached = input - cached - cache_write (floor 0).
output_tokens already includes reasoning_output_tokens; do not add reasoning again.

Long context: when a response's input_tokens > 272000 and the model lists long-context rates, use them; cached input in long context = 10% of the long-context input rate (assumption, not listed on the page).
cache_write null = the model has no separate cache-write price; bill those tokens as uncached input.
Fast mode (formerly priority) and batch are not detected; Standard tier is assumed.

Long-context cache write (assumption, not listed): the model's cache_write rate scaled by long-context input / input, which keeps the cache-write premium; a model without cache_write bills them as long-context uncached input.
Unpriced models (below) have no amount: their tokens are counted, the amount is left out of every total and the page says how many steps were skipped.
Local models (name contains '/' or ':' or starts with 'ollama') cost 0 and are marked as local.

_rules: usage.tokens = {input, output, cached, thoughts, tool}: input INCLUDES cached (total = input + output + thoughts + tool); uncached input = input - cached, billed at 'input'; cached is billed at 'cached_input'.
thoughts are billed at the output rate (the page labels output as including thinking tokens) and shown as part of output.

tool (tool-use prompt tokens) are billed as uncached input; the pricing page does not list them separately (assumption). Search grounding, explicit-cache storage and batch/flex/priority tiers are not detected; Standard tier text prices are used.
Models with per-modality prices (audio) are priced at the text/image/video rate: the session record does not split tokens by modality.
long_context: when the prompt (input + tool tokens) is above over_prompt_tokens the long-prompt rates apply to the whole request.
changes: dated rate changes announced on the pricing page; the latest entry whose 'from' date (UTC, from the message timestamp) has been reached replaces the base rates.
Models not in this table are unpriced (amount unknown, tokens still counted).
gemini.match: Strip a trailing date suffix such as -20251001 before lookup; names must otherwise match the model code on the pricing page exactly.

_rules: opencode runs models of many providers and has no price table of its own: a step is priced by its model name (provider prefixes such as anthropic/, Bedrock affixes and a date suffix are ignored) from the claude section, then the codex, gemini and other sections of this file (the other section holds every other vendor: xAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, Mistral, Qwen, ...), with those sections' own rules (tiers, long context, cache write rates, dated price changes).

Token fields per assistant message: tokens.input = uncached input, cache.read / cache.write = cached parts, output and reasoning are separate counts; billed output = output + reasoning (shown as 'output, of which reasoning').

For the codex and gemini sections (and, with the same meaning of input, the other section), input is rebuilt as input + cache read + cache write before their rules apply, because those sections expect input to include the cached parts; for the gemini section the reasoning tokens are passed as thoughts, and the UTC date of the message selects its dated price changes.
session.cost recorded by opencode is not used (it is often 0): every amount is computed from tokens and the prices above.
Models found in none of these sections are unpriced: their tokens are counted, the amount is left out of every total and the page says how many steps were skipped.

Providers named ollama, lmstudio or llama.cpp run on this machine and cost 0 (marked local). Other models served through a gateway (for example org/model) are not guessed: they stay unpriced unless the model name matches a table above.

Standard pay-as-you-go list prices in USD per million tokens of every vendor that has no section of its own, read from the vendor's own pricing page (the source field of each model; no aggregator prices). The models are found by name (the key or one of its aliases; gateway prefixes such as x-ai/ and a trailing -YYYYMMDD are ignored). Used for steps of tools that run models of many vendors (opencode).

Billing: uncached input x input + cache read x cached_input + cache write x cache_write + output x output. A missing cached_input or cache_write means the vendor lists no such rate: those tokens bill as uncached input. Output includes the reasoning tokens.

long_context: when the prompt (uncached input + cache read + cache write) is over over_input_tokens, the whole request is billed at the rates the long_context block lists (the other rates stay as they are).
changes: price changes the vendor has already announced, applied from the given UTC day on (the date of the message decides).

Peak / off-peak or sale prices: the standard (peak or listed) price is used and the note says what else the page shows, so an amount can be higher than the bill for off-peak use. Batch, priority, flex, free tiers, per-request search fees and subscription plans are not part of the estimate.

Models of these vendors that the official page does not list (retired, preview, open weights without a first-party price) are in unpriced: their tokens are counted, the amount is left out of every total and the page says how many steps were skipped. Names with a slash or a colon that no entry matches are treated as local models and cost 0.
